summary: Build practical water stewardship skills with risk tools, reporting methods, and a 12-month action roadmap. Enroll to strengthen resilience.
lede: Corporate water risk training helps professionals assess water exposure across operations, sites, suppliers and catchments. Designed for sustainability, ESG, operations, procurement and risk professionals, it provides a practical process for turning water findings into priorities and reporting. Participants practice basin screening, materiality assessment and risk-register design, then develop site reduction plans, supplier maps and a stewardship roadmap.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to assess corporate water exposure, translate technical findings into business priorities, and support credible reporting. It suits you if you work across sustainability, ESG, operations, compliance, procurement, or risk functions and need practical tools for water stewardship. Sustainability Managers who coordinate corporate water stewardship. ESG Managers who prepare water-related disclosures and metrics. Environmental Compliance Officers who track water obligations and controls. Operations Managers who manage site water reliability and usage. Facilities Managers responsible for water systems and efficiency. Supply Chain Risk Analysts who map supplier water dependencies. Environmental, Social and Governance Analysts who support reporting cycles. Corporate Affairs Managers handling water-related stakeholder communication. Health, Safety and Environment Specialists who monitor water incidents. Procurement Managers who align sourcing with water risk controls.
prerequisites: Bring a laptop with spreadsheet software, a willingness to work with site-level or supplier data, and any current water-related report, audit finding, or risk concern you want to test during exercises. Familiarity with environmental management concepts, ESG reporting cycles, or operations data will help you progress faster, but the course starts from practical foundations.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
